prompt:
Support has these reports about projects:

1. A workspace on the Free plan archived one of its two projects and still cannot create another: "the plan allows 2 projects".
2. Creating a project whose name begins like an existing one — "Web Visitors" next to "Web Vendors" — fails with "Something went wrong". The same happens when the look-alike project was archived long ago.
3. A new project was given the address of an archived project without complaint. Restoring the archived one afterwards fails with "Something went wrong".
4. Restoring an archived project let a Free workspace run three projects at once, and the projects meter on the billing page kept showing two until the periodic recount.
5. Restoring a project from a stale tab, when the project was not archived at all, reported success and left a "restored" entry behind.
6. Pausing or completing a project on its settings page looks saved, but the project is still shown as active afterwards and still accepts new issues. A project can be marked completed while it still has open issues.

Expected behaviour:

- Keys and addresses. Every project in a workspace has its own key, archived projects included — their issue numbers still carry it. When the key a project would get (chosen, or derived from the name) is already in use, it is made unique the way the address is: by appending a number, trimmed so the key never exceeds four characters. The address of an archived project stays reserved, so a new project asking for it gets a different one and the archived project can be restored under its own. Keys and addresses are per workspace.
- Plan slots. Only live projects count against the plan's project limit: archiving a project frees its slot at once and restoring it takes a slot again. Restoring is refused when the plan has no room for another project, and nothing is restored or announced. The workspace's projects meter follows immediately — after a restore it shows one more, and the periodic recount agrees with it — through any sequence of archiving and restoring.
- Restoring. Only an archived project can be restored; restoring one that is not archived is refused and announces nothing. A restored project comes back exactly as it was, with the status it had, and its archived issues stay archived.
- Status. A project is active, paused or completed; the status that is saved is the status the project has, and the project list's status filter reports it. New issues can be created only in an active project: a paused or completed project refuses them, nothing is created and nothing is announced, while its existing issues can still be worked on (status changes, comments) as before. A project can be marked completed only when none of its issues is open — done and canceled issues and archived issues are not open — however many issues it has; otherwise the request is refused and the project stays as it was. Marking it paused is always possible, and so is reactivating it. Marking a completed project completed again changes nothing. An archived project's status cannot be changed, and changing a status takes the same right as editing the project.

This is a `fix` task: edit the code and stop. Do not write a summary and do not emit an ANSWER line.
notes: Injected 3 defects in 1 file (bug.patch, project-repository): (a) countProjects counts archived rows too (comment: an archived project keeps its slot until the retention sweep purges it), so archiving never frees a slot; (b) updateProject drops the status column (comment: status reflects the project's issues, never a form value), so pausing or completing never sticks; (c) listTakenProjectSlugs returns live slugs only (comment: an archived address is free), so a new project can take an archived project's address and the restore then dies on projects_org_slug_idx. The create-project action's docstring (claiming archived projects occupy the quota) is misleading documentation left in place. Latent in pristine and described by the prompt: project keys are derived from the name (the form never lets the user choose one) and never made unique, so two projects whose names derive the same key hit projects_org_key_idx as a raw SqliteError, archived projects included; restoreProject neither checks that the project is archived (a live project is "restored" and project.restored is announced) nor the plan quota; the usage counters have no project.restored listener; the project status column has no semantics — a paused or completed project accepts issues and a project can be completed with open issues. Reference fix (9 files, 209 changed lines across lib, repositories, services and actions): lib/project-lifecycle (ProjectLifecycleError with code conflict and reasons not_active / open_issues / not_archived, acceptsNewIssues/assertAcceptsNewIssues), lib/errors (mapping + isDomainError), lib/slug (uniqueProjectKey: base, base2, base3 … trimmed to PROJECT_KEY_MAX_LENGTH = 4), project-repository (countProjects live only, listTakenProjectSlugs with archived rows again, listTakenProjectKeys over every row, updateProject writes status), issue-repository (countOpenIssues: live, status not done/canceled, a count rather than a page), project-service (keys made unique against every key in the workspace; completion gate on the count of open issues; restore refuses a live project and a full plan before writing and announcing), issue-service (assertAcceptsNewIssues after the archive and permission checks), usage-service (project.restored increments projectsUsed), create-project action docstring corrected. Why hard: six symptoms map onto three injected and five latent causes; the key collision surfaces as an internal error two layers above its cause, and the fix must consult archived rows (the natural "check the project list" consults live rows only); the restore has two causes behind one symptom (no quota check, no meter update) and the meter must stay right through archive/restore cycles; the status has an injected cause (not persisted) and a latent one (no gate), so reverting the injection alone leaves paused projects accepting issues; the completion gate must count every issue rather than read a page, which only shows past a hundred issues. Traps: scale (naive B, the completion gate reads the first page of 100 issues: fails "sees an open issue beyond the first hundred"); wrong place (naive C, keys made unique against the live project list: fails "keeps the key of an archived project reserved"); second cause (naive D, restore guarded by the archived check and the quota but the usage meter never hears about it: fails "moves the meter at once" and "consistent through archive, restore and archive again"). Hidden test: 21 cases, fake Date pinned to 2026-06-15T09:00Z, real id generator, logger and rate limiter, throwaway database built through the repositories; the 121-issue project is seeded through the repository. Validation: bug -> patch -p1 clean, tsc 0, visible 617/617; hidden 17/21 fail; bug+solution -> hidden 21/21 x3, full 638/638 x2, tsc 0; naive A (pristine, the three injected defects reverted and nothing else) 11/21 fail; naive B 1/21; naive C 1/21; naive D 2/21.
